subject: Patch validation handback & accelerated cadence for SIG review
messages:
From: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@finledger.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: evidence for CVE-2025-1234 remediation and patch validation

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As part of our SIG intake we're collecting concrete evidence for the CVE-2025-1234 fix (discovered in a third-party dependency). Can you please provide the following by EOD Friday so our internal audit can close the item: 

- Patch manifest (which hosts/services received the update; package versions + commit hashes)
- Staging test results that include regression runs for inference paths (tokenization, KV cache warm starts, streaming)
- A short signed attestation that the fix has been staged to prod canary and rollback playbook exists

We'd prefer artifacts as PDFs/CSV and a short note on scan cadence changes (if any). Attestation should reference SIG/CAIQ expectations.

If Friday is tight, let us know when you can turn this around. We may need a 15–20 minute call to confirm test artefacts with our security engineer.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Security Program Manager
FinLedger

---
Attachment stubs: none in initial request

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for CVE-2025-1234 remediation and patch validation

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. We have the artifacts ready and are bundling them into a compact evidence packet for SIG review. Quick summary up front:

- Fix deployed to canary on 2025-12-01 (canary footprint: 5% of requests in us-west-2)
- Patch manifest attached (patch-manifest-20251203.csv) — includes containers, image tags, and commit SHA references (sha256:9f7b...).
- Staging test report attached (staging-test-report-CVE-2025-1234.pdf) — unit, integration, and a 2-hour load regression that validates KV cache integrity and streaming latency under synthetic traffic.
- Signed attestation (signed-attestation-kp-20251203.pdf) — I signed and timestamped it; attestation references our remediation SLA and rollback playbook.

Operational notes: we've increased VM/third-party dependency scans from a monthly to a weekly cadence for the dependency group that produced the vulnerability; this is reflected in the report index and in the header of the patch manifest. We also updated our SOC2 evidence folder with the updated scan schedule.

I've attached the three artefacts and dropped a Drive link and the JIRA ticket (JIRA-SEC-4719) below. If you want screenshots from the canary rollout (histograms of error rates and latency) I can add a short appendix.

Let us know if the file formats are acceptable or if you want the manifest in JSON instead of CSV.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: patch-manifest-20251203.csv (text/csv), staging-test-report-CVE-2025-1234.pdf (application/pdf), signed-attestation-kp-20251203.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@finledger.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 13:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for CVE-2025-1234 remediation and patch validation

Hi Sarah —

Quick note to confirm the CSV manifest includes the staging and prod canary image tags and the exact A/B group IDs we used during the rollout. I also added a short checksum column for each artifact so you can verify integrity (sha256 values included).

We ran an additional acceptance test overnight to validate streaming fallback behavior — results are in the PDF under section 4.2. If you want, I can extract that section into a one-page summary for auditors.

Ben, fyi — I updated the weekly scan schedule in the SOC2 evidence drive and added a short changelog that maps to our remediation SLA (30 days for moderate, 7 days for high).

Marissa
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Forwarded excerpt from staging-test-report-CVE-2025-1234.pdf:
"Acceptance test (12/03/2025 02:10Z): streaming continuity preserved; no observed token loss during KV cache warm starts; 99.9th latency percentile unchanged within measurement error margin."

From: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@finledger.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 08:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for CVE-2025-1234 remediation and patch validation

Kimberly / Marissa —

Received the packet and the attachments. Reviewed the manifest and the acceptance excerpt; the checksum column was helpful. For SIG/CAIQ closure we need one small addition: a short line in the attestation that explicitly states the timeline for customer-facing production rollout (even if it is a staged canary) and the defined rollback window (e.g., 30 minutes). Can you add that and return an updated signed-attestation.pdf?

A 15-minute call tomorrow morning to walk through the staging test semantics would also be useful — do either of you have availability at 09:30 PT? If yes, please send a calendar invite and we'll add our security engineer (cc'd in security@finledger.com).

Once we have the updated attestation we can finalize the SIG response. Thanks for the timely turnaround on this.

Best,
Sarah
Security Program Manager
FinLedger

---
Attachments reviewed: patch-manifest-20251203.csv, staging-test-report-CVE-2025-1234.pdf, signed-attestation-kp-20251203.pdf
